scored.name: Stove-side child fireguard, BS 8423 tested
scored.moat_mechanism: Independent BS 8423 test report + EU registered design (fold profile); credibility mark, not a legal barrier
scored.reasoning: Price EUR 79-119 with ~EUR 33 landed gives ~3x and room to absorb CAC; Google intent search plus housing-association/daycare B2B is credible. Moat is soft: BS 8423 is a UK standard, SE/DK acceptance unverified, copycat can pay the same fee, and a registered design only blocks lookalikes. Bulky freight and fire-safety liability are the risks. Capital ~EUR 5-7.5k plus ~1.5k tooling is inside soft limits.

scored.name: Roof-window / tall-window child-safety stopper 2-pack
scored.moat_mechanism: EN 13126-5/EN 16281 certification (competitors must pay same test) + EU registered design; B2B 10-pack via ex-VELUX/housing association network
scored.reasoning: Best founder fit (roof windows, installers, associations) and a regulatory pull from Boverket's 2.0 m rule. 2-pack at EUR 35-45 vs ~EUR 8-14 landed gives ~70% GM, B2B packs give low CAC. Moat is limited: Habo/ASSA already hold EN 13126-5 and the roof-window gap and Danish rules are unverified; certification protects only credibility. Tooling EUR 2-3.5k and first order EUR 2.5-4k plus test are within soft limits. Product-liability exposure for a child-safety device needs insurance.

scored.name: Retrofit window air vent with EN 13141-1 data
scored.moat_mechanism: Test reports (airflow/acoustic) + registered design; B2B installer channel; weakest moat of set
scored.reasoning: Established incumbents (Flexit, Biobe, Renson, Titon) and the idea itself calls its moat the weakest. Extrusion die EUR 2.5-4.5k is borderline and test fees per variant plus first order could push all-in to ~EUR 10k. Margin is fine (EUR 29-45 vs 6-10 landed) and the building-industry B2B channel is a real edge, but ventilation is performance- and regulation-sensitive (building-code acceptance), and no demand or price data were found.

scored.name: Modular outdoor step anti-slip tread, DIN 51130
scored.moat_mechanism: DIN 51130 R-class + frost/salt ageing test, registered design for interlock; B2B housing associations
scored.reasoning: Real winter-fall problem and an association channel, but a test report is cheap for rivals and imported mats can add one. Landed EUR 14-20 vs EUR 39-59 retail is only ~2.5-3x, and rubber is heavy/bulky to ship. Tooling EUR 2.5-4k plus EUR 4-6k first order is acceptable but all-in near EUR 10k. Seasonal; must land before October so 2026 is already missed.

scored.name: DIN 51097 class C bath/shower mat
scored.moat_mechanism: Paid DIN 51097 report + registered design; professional class C mats already exist
scored.kill_reason: Hard kill: bath/shower mats are an Amazon private-label/commodity category; class C mats already sold by Kaiserkraft/EHA, and press-mould tooling of EUR 2.5-4k for a weak moat
scored.reasoning: Amazon private-label dominated category and the test report is a cheap, copyable differentiator. Care-home B2B exists but the founders have no edge there. Killed on the private-label hard rule.

scored.name: Ice-rescue and skating safety kit
scored.moat_mechanism: Only if exclusive SLS/Sjoraddningssallskapet endorsement is won (unconfirmed); otherwise none
scored.reasoning: A bundle of commodity parts (Jula isdubbar SEK 99.90, throw lines EUR 28-30) with the endorsement unconfirmed, so no moat. Low capital (EUR 2.5-3.5k) is its only merit. ~3x landed margin at EUR 49-69 but paid CAC on a seasonal product with no founder channel; life-safety claims add liability.

scored.name: Cordless retrofit for roof-window pleated blinds (EN 16434)
scored.moat_mechanism: EN 16434 test + registered design/utility model on handle; fit-by-model know-how (not legal)
scored.reasoning: Founder know-how helps, but demand evidence is nil, OEM compatibility is unverified, the window maker can respond, and injection mould of EUR 3-5k is at the limit. Price EUR 25-39 is below the CAC-friendly threshold; installer/association channel partly compensates. Child-safety liability applies.

scored.name: Nordic Sun-Path Instrument (latitude brass desk object)
scored.moat_mechanism: EU registered design + per-latitude calibration/numbered editions + B2B network (architects/installers); easily CNC-copied
scored.reasoning: EUR 99 at ~EUR 30 landed gives ~3.3x and ~70% GM, high enough price to absorb some CAC, and the daylight story fits the ex-VELUX background; professional gifting is a plausible low-CAC channel. Moat is design registration plus channel only; a CNC shop copies it. Niche demand, no search data, price unverified. Total capital ~EUR 8-9k all-in is within soft limits.

scored.name: Estate-licensed reissue of small Nordic mid-century object
scored.moat_mechanism: Exclusive copyright/design licence from estate of designer; enforceable by licensor
scored.reasoning: Exclusive licence is a genuine mechanism and the reissue wave is documented, but no available estate/object has been identified and the legal basis is unverified, so I cap defensibility at 3 until a licence is signed. Founders' negotiation/sourcing/design edge matches the work. Margin ~3.5x at EUR 79, minus royalties; collectible drops give some repeat. All-in ~EUR 9-10.5k is at the soft ceiling.

scored.name: Exclusive-artist wooden jigsaw puzzle
scored.moat_mechanism: Exclusive 3-year artist licence for puzzle category + numbered editions
scored.reasoning: Licence is a real but time-limited moat (artist can leave after term; format generic). Premium wooden puzzles sell at EUR 42-80, so EUR 79 is at the top and unproven. Artist audience co-marketing lowers CAC, and collectors add repeat. Capital ~EUR 7-8k first order, tooling small. No artist secured.

scored.name: Annual numbered Advent-candle holder series
scored.moat_mechanism: Annual artist-edition series habit + registered design; builds only after 2-3 editions
scored.reasoning: Series model gives repeat but the moat is absent for edition 1 and annual artist deals are not exclusive against copyists. Single seasonal window and first launch is Advent 2027, so cash is tied up ~a year. EUR 85 at ~EUR 24 landed is ~3.5x; first order EUR 7-7.5k plus fees plus tooling approaches EUR 10k. Open-flame candle product needs GPSR checks.

scored.name: Brf / housing-association door-sign system with inserts
scored.moat_mechanism: B2B channel (founders' housing-association relationships) + spec lock-in per building + registered design
scored.reasoning: Lowest CAC route of the set if the pilot works (one Brf = 20-100 units) and inserts recur with move-ins, but demand and price are unvalidated and signage makers abound. Bulk EUR 39-45 vs ~EUR 17 landed is only ~2.4x (58% GM); DTC set EUR 59 is better. Spec lock-in is real but modest. Requires pilot with friendly boards before ordering; capital ~EUR 6-7.5k all-in.

scored.name: Winter-bathing club-edition dip kit
scored.moat_mechanism: Club-specific engraved editions (switching cost, pre-sold MOQ) + registered design; weak
scored.reasoning: Strong growth in winter bathing (70k+ DK members) but easy to copy and the founders have no club relationships. Club editions pre-sold in 50+ batches offer low CAC if committees commit; price EUR 39-45 at EUR 12-15 landed is ~3x. Capital is modest (EUR 3.6-4.5k); only order after 5+ club commitments.

scored.name: Stone-Sill Care Kit for housing associations
scored.moat_mechanism: B2B handover-pack lock-in via Brf care sheets + optional lab etch/pH test; no IP
scored.reasoning: Documented care sheets prescribe soap and paraffin oil, so there is a named spec to standardise and consumable repeat; handover packs avoid paid CAC. But the contents are commodity (a Brf can buy Grumme soap itself), bulk EUR 19-24 vs EUR 7-10 landed is only ~2.4x, and the buyer's willingness to pay for a branded bundle is unproven. Low capital (~EUR 5-7k). Good founder-channel fit.

scored.name: Corten Calm run-off stabiliser
scored.moat_mechanism: Contract-blender formulation exclusivity + run-off staining test; claim unproven
scored.reasoning: High-margin consumable (EUR 32-39 vs 6-9 landed, re-coat every 1-2 years) but the performance claim is untested, chemists copy formulations quickly, and chemical products add CLP/REACH labelling and liquid shipping. Test cost EUR 1-2.5k is spent before knowing if it works. Landscaper B2B channel is not a founder strength.

scored.name: Cut-End Seal Kit for decking/cladding installers
scored.moat_mechanism: None beyond installer-spec adoption; optional design registration
scored.reasoning: A commodity sealer that merchants already stock; installer price EUR 15-18 vs EUR 5-7 landed gives only ~2.5-3x. Repeat and low-CAC installer route help, but no moat and retail price is under the EUR 35 preference. Low capital.

scored.name: WaxCartridge twist-up refill applicator
scored.moat_mechanism: Registered design on applicator/cartridge profile + cartridge-only consumable; rivals can launch incompatible stick
scored.reasoning: Refill margin is excellent (EUR 14-17 vs 3.5-5 landed) but use is infrequent (~10 garments per 100 g block) and the lock-in only starts after a starter sale; the mechanism is a design right, not a utility right. Starter EUR 29-35 barely absorbs CAC with no B2B channel. Tooling EUR 3-4.5k plus EUR 7.5-9k first order is near the combined ceiling for weak evidence.

scored.name: Roof-Window Frame Refinish Kit
scored.moat_mechanism: None; installer channel only; OEM sells own repair lacquer
scored.reasoning: Founder channel fits and capital is low, but OEM already sells its own lacquer, there is no IP, brand/non-compete risk, and installer pricing (EUR 19-24 vs EUR 8-11 landed) is only ~2.3x. Re-lacquer cycles give mild repeat.

scored.name: Awning & cab-canvas refill pouch system
scored.moat_mechanism: None meaningful; lab water-repellency test and pouch format
scored.reasoning: Biltema, Bauhaus and Dickson are entrenched; no founder channel and high CAC risk. Registrations are rising but caravan base is falling. Refills give repeat but the idea itself calls it the weakest. Capital EUR 5-6.5k is sizeable for no moat.

scored.name: FrostSafe self-draining rain-barrel diverter
scored.moat_mechanism: German utility model (unexamined) + EU registered design; freedom-to-operate vs thermostatic drain valves unchecked
scored.reasoning: A functional mechanism is the only concept here with a genuine patent-type angle, but utility models are unexamined, FTO is unknown, and passive thermal-drain reliability is unproven (returns and freeze-failure risk). Tooling EUR 3-4.5k + IP ~EUR 0.4k plus EUR 4.5-6k first order totals ~EUR 8-11k, heavy for weak evidence. Allotment group-buys are plausible low-CAC but unbuilt. Seasonal.

scored.name: Rodent-proof seasonal crawl-space vent set
scored.moat_mechanism: Utility model + registered design on rodent-proof closure; merchant/installer channel
scored.reasoning: Large cabin base (634k fritidshus) and a 6-vent set at EUR 99-139 absorbs CAC, with ~75% GM. Closable crawl-space vents already exist, so novelty rests on the unverified rodent-proof closure; design-around is easy. Builders' merchants are a relationship channel but sell-in is slow. Tooling EUR 2.5-4k plus first order EUR 3.5-5k is acceptable.

scored.name: Cabin well/lake-water filter with keyed cartridge
scored.moat_mechanism: Consumable lock-in: keyed bayonet cartridge + registered design on cap/cartridge
scored.reasoning: Real consumable lock-in with ~3.7x cartridge margin and refill subscription, but clones of a keyed cartridge are plausible, food-contact (1935/2004) testing and drinking-water claims add regulatory risk, and EUR 7-9.5k first order plus EUR 3.5-5k tooling is ~EUR 12-14k all-in, beyond the intended soft envelope without validated demand. Not killed because each limit is individually within bounds.

scored.name: Van cab thermal screens, scanned patterns
scored.moat_mechanism: Pattern library know-how + registered design on clip; copyable by scanning
scored.reasoning: Low capital (EUR 2.5-4.5k), high ticket (EUR 89-149) absorbs CAC, and UK sellers add import friction. But landed EUR 30-45 gives only ~3x at best, per-chassis SKU complexity raises inventory and returns risk, and a copycat can scan the same vans. Registrations growth partly dealer pre-registration for Euro 6.

scored.name: Closable sauna ventilation kit
scored.moat_mechanism: Registered design only; B2B via building network unproven for saunas
scored.reasoning: Niche, weak moat (admitted), Bauhaus already sells plate valves, and tooling EUR 2.5-3.5k for a commodity part. Margin decent (EUR 39-59 vs 10-15 landed) and DIY forum demand is visible, but no founder sauna channel and paid CAC likely exceeds contribution.
